output.brief: The evidence does not support the drafted claim. The shared platform's audit trail shows the architect answered 62 of 64 queries on time. The 41 "late" queries in the claim come from the contractor's own draft dates. 39 of them sat in Callerby's draft status for 9–47 days before being sent. The change orders were mostly small interior items. The one structural change, CO-09, was issued on 6 November. The crane left site in October, and the superintendent says the steel was on the ground. The most likely main driver is Callerby's own decision to send the crane and frame gang to Kestrel. CO-09 may have added some delay, and I could not size it. I'm fairly sure about the query data and less sure about the split of blame. Do not submit the claim as drafted: it rests on misleading figures and risks credibility and a counterclaim. Don't withdraw it or settle yet either. Next steps: (1) commission an independent delay analysis, using the platform timestamps, crane ledger and site diaries, to measure any genuine CO-09 delay; (2) check how Fenmore's 6% success fee shaped its analysis; (3) don't discipline the superintendent, who answered honestly; (4) review how the crane transfer was approved, but don't blame the incentive scheme without evidence.
